closes: First AR(1)-autocorrelation characterization of estimated-parameter ARL0 for all three module detector arms (Shewhart, EWMA, CUSUM).

First measurement of the module's locked >=90% seeded-shift recall target under estimated (short-window) limits AND AR(1) autocorrelated data, via a 128-case tamper corpus with tampers masked as sensor noise.
does_not_close: Does NOT establish real-batch acceptability, product qualification, EHS acceptability, or batch-release authority.
Non-normality (only Gaussian AR(1) innovations are modeled) remains open.
MA/ARMA and higher-order AR autocorrelation structures are not modeled.
No prospective time-ordered 30-batch pilot is checked in; this is a theory + Monte-Carlo characterization on owned synthetic data.
The tamper corpus uses one realization per case (not a resampled MC estimate per case); recall is a corpus-level rate over 128 independent draws, not a per-case confidence interval.

known_parameter_anchor_gate.note: ARL0 is defined as the MEAN in-control run length (not the median, which for a geometric-shaped run-length distribution sits near mean*ln(2)); compared against measured_arl0_mean at m=100000, phi=0 (known-parameter regime), horizon-censored mean is a conservative (low-biased) estimator.

model: X_t = mu + phi*(X_{t-1}-mu) + eps_t, eps_t~N(0,sigma^2*(1-phi^2)); mu_hat/sigma_hat estimated NAIVELY (sample mean / sample sd, ddof=1) from the m-length baseline, exactly as the module's iid-assuming implementation does; no AR(1) correction exists in the live capability.

part_a_m50_budget_check.note: m=50 was reported by mr-memory-detector-arl-degradation-v1 / the consolidated KPI as the smallest baseline that STILL MEETS the locked false-alarm budget, under the i.i.d. (phi=0) assumption.

purpose: Test whether the module's estimated-parameter ARL characterization (five prior evidence/audit/*-arl-degradation-v1 receipts, all i.i.d.-only) and its locked >=90% seeded-shift recall target survive AR(1) autocorrelated in-control data and tampers masked as sensor noise.
